attachments.name: Scope 1.5x
attachments.effect:
The ACOG Sight is a weapon attachment featured in Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege.

From the duration of Operation Shadow Legacy expansion to Operation Deep Freeze, Sights of various zoom levels had been introduced: the Scope 1.5x, Scope 2x , Scope 2.5x (formerly ACOG), and Scope 3x.

Starting from Operation Deadly Omen, the zoom level of 1.5x and 2.0x had been removed, along with the general rework of Scope mechanics. The design of 1.5 was repurposed into 2.5x zoom, and 2.0 into Telescopic with 3.5x zoom level.

attachments.name: Angled Grip
attachments.effect:
The Angled Grip is a weapon attachment featured in Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege.

The Angled Grip decreases (by 32%) the time to change from hip fire into ADS (Aiming Down the Sight), especially during the sprint animation. It is extremely useful for players that engage enemies in close-quarter firefights. However, it doesn't improve recoil control, unlike its vertical counterpart.

attachments.name: Compensator
attachments.effect:
The Compensator is a weapon attachment featured in Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege. It reduces the horizontal recoil by 35%.

The Recoil Diamond is the individual points of a recoil pattern when aiming down sight, reducing the randomization of bullet patterns during muzzle climb. The shape of the muzzle climb differs between guns, some being taller, others wider, therefore a reduction of the diamond makes the climb straighter and more predictable.

This attachment is best used for weapons with inherently low vertical recoil, and are used for close to medium range combat.

attachments.name: Extended Barrel
attachments.effect:
The Extended Barrel is a weapon attachment featured in Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege.

===Overview=== Contrary to the in-game description, the damage drop-off for any weapon that has the Extended Barrel attached starts at the exact same distance. This means that the Extended Barrel does not provide full power over a greater distance. Instead, damage drop-off is reduced by 15-20%.

While the Extended Barrel has no discernable effect on recoil, equipping it does involve missing out on other potentially recoil-reducing attachments. Because most gunfights occur in short-to-medium range, the usefulness of the Extended Barrel is rather questionable in most situations. In addition, the attachment increases the physical length of the weapon considerably, making it easier for enemies to spot the operator when peeking around a corner.

attachments.name: Flash Hider
attachments.effect:
The Flash Hider is a weapon attachment featured in Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege. It hides the muzzle flash of weapons so the enemy may take longer to notice where the shot come from. Every time the weapon starts firing, it slightly reduces the vertical recoil and greatly reduces the horizontal recoil for the first 3 shots. Internally, the Flash Hider reduces first shot vertical recoil by approximately 13% and overall vertical recoil by approximately 15%.

Unlike the Muzzle Brake which only reduces first shot vertical recoil, the Flash Hider's effects will last throughout the entire spray, much like the Vertical Grip. This means that the Flash Hider is most effective when used on fully-automatic weapons.

attachments.name: Flashlight
attachments.effect:
Barrel The Flashlight is a weapon attachment in Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege that was featured in the Outbreak event.

The attachment was available by default on all available weapons in the event. It allowed players the option to turn it on or off. This gave players increased visibility or discretion against enemies.

attachments.name: Holographic Sight
attachments.effect:
MH1 = The Holographic Sight is a non-magnifying optical attachment featured in Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege.

Similar to the Red Dot Sight, it replaces the default iron sight and provides a better line of sight for players to engage enemies from afar.

===Variants=== Four variants of the Holographic Sight are available: NATO, Russian, Razor, and the MH1. With the release of the Demon Veil expansion, all variants are available on all weapons that are capable of attaching a Holographic Sight. *The NATO Holograhpic Sight, designated in-game as the Holo A, is less obtrusive in the center but obstructs more peripheral vision in ADS compared to the Red Dot Sight. *The Russian Holograhpic Sight, designated in-game as the Holo B, shows a circular crosshair without a top bar, while the "usual" version shows a much smaller red dot with a circle around the target. *The Razor Holograhpic Sight, designated in-game as the Holo C, features a thinner casing and a slightly thicker reticle compared to the NATO Variant. *The MH1 Holograhpic Sight, designated in-game as the Holo D, has a similarly-sized casing compared to the NATO variant, but a completely different reticle with a dot in the middle

attachments.name: Laser
attachments.effect:
Barrel The Laser is a weapon attachment featured in Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege. It tightens a weapon's hip fire accuracy and a shotgun pellet's spread by 25%, though it can also reveal a player's position if the red dot emitted from the light is noticed by the opposing team.

The laser originally created a faint but visible red laser beam, making it relatively easy to deduce the player's location once a laser is spotted. However, the laser was changed to only leave a red laser dot at the surface it is aiming at instead, which made spotting the dot and deducing the player's location more difficult.

When aiming down sight, the laser dot disappears from the user's perspective. However, it will remain visible to other players.

attachments.name: Muzzle Brake
attachments.effect:
The Muzzle Brake is a weapon attachment featured in Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege. It greatly reduces the vertical recoil and does not change a weapons horizontal recoil similar to the Compensator and Flash Hider.

The Muzzle Brake reduces the recoil of the first shot by 45%, along with a 45% reduction for the re-centering time after shots.

Re-centering time refers to the time it takes for the crosshair to returned to the point at which the player was initially aiming, after the weapon has kicked up due to recoil. Regardless of how far up the recoil has kicked the gun, be it one bullet or ten, this duration is fixed. Thus, the Muzzle Break reduces this time by 45%. Re-centering only takes place after the weapon has stopped firing.

attachments.name: Red Dot Sight
attachments.effect:
M4S The Red Dot Sight is a non-magnifying optical attachment featured in Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege. It replaces the default iron sight and provides a better line of sight for players to engage enemies from afar.

It is available on all primary weapons except the CSRX 300 as well as a select few secondary weapons.

===Variants=== Four variants of the RDS are available: NATO, Russian, M4S, and Handgun. With the release of the Demon Veil expansion, three of the variants are available on all weapons that are capable of attaching a Red Dot Sight. *The NATO Red Dot, designated in-game as Red Dot A, comes with a thick, somewhat obstrusive casing, and a simple reticle in the form of a dot. The dot on the NATO variant is somewhat big and can, to an extent, block line of sight on the object aimed at. The NATO variant also comes with a riser attached on specific weapons to avoid obstruction of vision when aiming down sights. *The Russian Red Dot Sight, designated in-gane as Red Dot B which is notably smaller than the NATO Red Dot Sight, and features a thin casing but a more complicated reticle. *The M4S Red Dot Sight, designated in-game as Red Dot C, was introduced in the Operation Shado

attachments.name: Suppressor
attachments.effect:
The Suppressor is a weapon attachment featured in Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege. It greatly reduces the sound emitted from a weapon when fired. Due to the importance of listening to one's surroundings to determine the location of the enemy, the suppressor is extremely valuable in masking the player's location as a result. This can be useful in dispatching lone enemies in Training Grounds or multiplayer as well as destroying surveillance cameras.

Missed bullets fired from a suppressed weapon do not trigger a white threat indicator, nor will they create smoke trails. If a shot lands on a target they will experience no indicators telling them where the shot came from. While a normal weapon can be heard from across the map in the open, a suppressed weapon can only be heard from 30 meters away. The Suppressor hides the muzzle flash of weapons better than a Flash Hider does, but cannot bring any recoil benefits.

Almost every in-game weapon can be equipped with a suppressor. However, there are exceptions.
